title: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia ATRA dosing and favourable risk AML with transplant decisions

steps.tx: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia (a marrow cancer of abnormal promyelocytes) carries **t(15;17)** fusing **PML** with **RARA** (retinoic acid receptor alpha), which freezes white cell maturation and triggers DIC (disseminated intravascular coagulation, body wide clotting and bleeding). **ATRA** (all trans retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative) unblocks the receptor and forces the blasts to mature into working neutrophils instead of killing them outright.
steps.say: Promyelocytic leukaemia looks terrifying at presentation, with bleeding from every puncture site, but its genetics point to an elegant cure. The swapped chromosomes jam the vitamin A receptor so young white cells cannot grow up. ATRA, a concentrated vitamin A cousin, releases that jam and orders the leukemic cells to finish maturing into harmless neutrophils. That is why this leukaemia melts away without the usual cell killing drugs.

vis.alt: Illustration of myeloblasts with Auer rods and faggot cells, the t(15;17) PML RARA fusion, and ATRA therapy effect.
vis.caption: Faggot cells and PML::RARA behind ATRA driven maturation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Adults receive oral ATRA (generic tretinoin) **45 mg per square metre per day** in two divided doses every 12 hours until complete remission, paired with intravenous arsenic trioxide **0.15 mg per kg per day** in low and intermediate risk disease (white cells 10,000 or less), which cures without chemotherapy in the APL0406 protocol. Children and adolescents under 20 years receive a reduced **25 mg per square metre per day** to lower pseudotumour cerebri (a dangerous rise in brain pressure mimicking a tumour).
steps.say: The dosing schedule for ATRA requires careful age-adjusted precision. Adults take forty five milligrams per square metre daily, split morning and evening, continuing until complete bone marrow remission, alongside daily arsenic infusions for lower risk disease. Pediatric patients under twenty receive twenty five milligrams per square metre, because standard adult doses cause intracranial hypertension. Arsenic dosing is calculated by body weight rather than surface area.

steps.tx: AML with **t(8;21)** fusing **RUNX1** with **RUNX1T1** (core binding factor leukaemia with M2 morphology) shows slender Auer rods (needle like granules), salmon pink granules and aberrant CD19 or CD56 markers, yet carries **favourable** risk with about 90% remission. Consolidation uses high dose cytarabine (HiDAC) plus gemtuzumab ozogamicin, with no upfront transplant. Never confuse this fusion with a RUNX1 point mutation, which is adverse risk.
steps.say: This translocation presents a striking clinical contrast between morphology and prognosis. Under the microscope it appears aggressive, displaying prominent Auer rods and aberrant lymphoid markers, yet genetically it belongs to the most favourable risk category, curing approximately nine in ten patients with chemotherapy alone. High dose cytarabine provides definitive consolidation without upfront transplant. Crucially, distinguish this favourable fusion from an isolated RUNX1 point mutation, which confers adverse risk.

vis.alt: Stained blood smear showing a myeloblast packed with needle like Auer rods.
vis.caption: Auer rods of the kind seen in favourable t(8;21) AML. Image: Ed Uthman, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: The second core binding factor leukaemia, **inv(16)** fusing **CBFB** with **MYH11** (M4 with abnormal eosinophils), shares the favourable outlook and HiDAC consolidation. Both core binding subtypes gain extra benefit from **gemtuzumab ozogamicin** (an antibody delivering toxin to CD33 positive blasts). A high burden **KIT mutation** (a growth receptor gene) or lingering MRD (measurable residual disease) erases the advantage and pushes the patient toward transplant.
steps.say: Pair the two core binding leukaemias together in memory. The chromosome sixteen inversion shows its own giveaway, abnormal eosinophils alongside blasts, and enjoys the same excellent cure rate with high dose cytarabine. Both types welcome the CD33 targeted antibody gemtuzumab. But two red flags cancel the good news: a heavy KIT mutation burden or hidden disease surviving chemotherapy, either of which redirects the patient to transplant.

steps.tx: **Allogeneic transplant** (marrow from a donor) in first remission is standard for **intermediate** and **adverse** risk AML under ELN 2022 (European LeukemiaNet guidance), because chemotherapy alone relapses too often. **Favourable** risk AML skips upfront transplant and takes chemotherapy consolidation, except when persistent MRD (measurable disease staying positive) or a high KIT burden appears, which upgrade the patient to the transplant pathway.
steps.say: Transplant timing follows risk like a rulebook. Middle and bad risk leukaemias proceed to donor transplant during their first remission without debate, since drugs alone cannot hold them. Good risk leukaemias skip that ordeal and finish with chemotherapy, unless follow up testing finds surviving disease or a dangerous KIT mutation. Those two findings promote a good risk patient into the transplant queue.
